newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds were spared a rough ride on Wednesday and closed only slightly weaker, unlike Europe high-yielders which made big losses. Guilders also outperformed German debt as demand outpaced offers by almost two to one.
The market had to settle for modest losses at the end of the day, partly tracking bund futures which fell after data showing U.S. real earnings rose faster than expected in September.
U.S. CPI data earlier in the day came in exactly as forecast and failed to give the market the stir it was braced for.
"Despite the lower close we have performed well," one trader said, adding the 10-year discount to Germany had widened.
The 10-year Dutch-German spread widened to 13 basis points from 10.
Fresh EMU pessimism in Italy set off by Bundesbank president Tietmeyer triggered a free fall there and dealers noted switches to hardcore currencies such as the guilder.
Also, the curve flattened by two basis points as the very short end of 1998-1999 paper seemed a bit out of favour after having rallied in the last two to three weeks.
Yields at the very short end of the curve fell by 20 basis points in recent weeks, clearly outperforming longer maturities despite their already low levels.
Fresh demand by institutions, which came on stream after a very sluggish start, helped underpin the market and dealers were optimistic about further gains.

While traders were switching from the middle end of the curve, around 2002, and overall shortening durations, investors should be looking at 30-year bonds as the spread with 10-year paper was at historic highs, one trader said.
